title: Over $600 Million in Polymarket Election Trades Took Place After Races Ended
gist: Two Polymarket election markets (Ethiopia and Romania among them) generated over $600 million in volume, mostly in pairs of accounts trading with each other on long-shot candidates after outcomes were effectively known. Experts call it wash trading or 'activity farming' for a possible Polymarket token airdrop, raising questions about volume as a growth metric for a $21 billion-valued platform.

insights.claim: Two global election markets on Polymarket's offshore platform generated over $600 million in trading volume, far more than most political markets, with most activity in contracts tied to long-shot candidates who did not win.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Headline volume on Polymarket can be dominated by non-economic activity, so treat volume as an unreliable signal of real interest.
insights.locator: Two global election markets on Polymarket’s offshore platform

insights.claim: In Ethiopia's summer election, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's Prosperity Party won 438 seats against 13 for the closest rival, yet only $173,000 was wagered on Ahmed winning versus over $41 million on his chief of staff Shimelis Abdisa becoming leader, with over $285 million traded in total, nearly all on losing candidates.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Volume inversely related to odds is a red flag for manipulation; use it as a screen for unreliable prediction-market prices.
insights.locator: This summer, Ethiopian prime minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party

insights.claim: About $284 million of the Ethiopia market volume came from pairs of accounts repeatedly buying and selling with each other, according to former Polymarket trader Chris Park of forensic firm MSR Decode.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Nearly all volume being self-dealing means reported market activity on this contract was almost entirely artificial.
insights.quote: Nearly all of it—about $284 million—came from pairs of accounts repeatedly buying and selling with each other

insights.claim: Polymarket's rules kept the Ethiopia market open until the prime minister was formally appointed in October, so it stayed live for several months after the result was foregone, with bursts of irrational trading continuing for 123 days after the election.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Resolution rules that leave decided markets open create 'zombie' contracts that can be exploited, a product-design weakness to watch.
insights.locator: The timing of these trades made things even weirder

insights.claim: Polymarket's head of global intelligence says the team immediately flagged and blocked the accounts, but the company did not explain why the accounts could trade such high volume before action was taken.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Detection and enforcement lag is an open question for platform integrity and for regulators.
insights.locator: When asked about these markets, Shana Bautista

insights.claim: Barnard economist Rajiv Sethi calls markets where people can trade on events that have already happened or are no longer happening 'zombie markets', and sees the Ethiopia volume as obvious volume manipulation.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: A reusable lens for screening prediction-market contracts: stale or already-decided markets are prone to manipulation.
insights.quote: It's obviously some form of volume manipulation
insights.locator: Such a high volume of seemingly pointless back-and-forth

insights.claim: In a Romanian 2024 election market that Polymarket left running alongside the rerun vote after the original election was annulled, Sethi's wash-trading detection algorithm flagged nearly all volume as suspicious, with 99.6 percent of volume for certain weeks being wash trading.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Repeated pattern across two countries suggests systematic rather than one-off abuse on the offshore platform.
insights.quote: 99.6 percent of volume in this market for certain weeks has been wash trading
insights.locator: Another market about a 2024 election in Romania

insights.claim: Wash trading, in which accounts repeatedly trade to create the illusion of heavy activity, is banned on regulated US exchanges and prohibited in Polymarket's terms of service, and an earlier Sethi study found widespread wash trading on Polymarket's offshore platform.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Offshore venue lacks the surveillance of regulated exchanges, a regulatory arbitrage and credibility risk.
insights.locator: Wash trading is a type of market manipulation

insights.claim: Sethi cautions that because trader identities are unknown, apparent wash trading is not always wash trading, leaving uncertainty about the Ethiopian and Romanian markets.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Attribution is hard on pseudonymous venues; avoid treating suspected wash trading as proven.
insights.quote: What appears to be wash trading isn't always wash trading
insights.locator: Wash trading could explain what happened

insights.claim: MSR Decode concluded the most likely explanation for the Ethiopian anomaly is 'activity farming', with traders inflating volume because they expect to benefit if Polymarket launches a cryptocurrency token.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Anticipation of a Polymarket token distorts its volume metrics; the token launch is a catalyst and the volume may be an artifact of airdrop speculation.
insights.locator: MSR Decode ran an analysis of the Ethiopian market for WIRED

insights.claim: Polymarket chief marketing officer Matthew Modabber said in 2025 on a crypto-themed podcast there 'would be a token' without specifics, and Sethi finds it plausible that higher-volume accounts hope for token allocation.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: An unconfirmed token creates a farming incentive; watch for an official launch announcement and eligibility rules.

insights.claim: MSR Decode analysed over 38,000 post-election trade loops in the Ethiopia market and found over 98 percent resulted in neither side gaining or losing money, with a median holding time of nine seconds, which makes sophisticated profit-seeking algorithms unlikely.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Zero-PnL, seconds-long loops are consistent with volume farming, not alpha-seeking trade.
insights.locator: When MSR Decode analyzed the Ethiopian election market

insights.claim: University researcher Andre Guettler describes the behaviour as textbook examples of how market participants farm a potential airdrop, a pattern previously seen in the cryptocurrency industry.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Airdrop-farming behaviour inflates headline metrics; discount volume for any platform expected to issue a token.
insights.quote: These are textbook examples on how market participants farm a potential airdrop
insights.locator: This type of behavior has been observed before

insights.claim: Polymarket recently raised over $1 billion led by 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner, at an estimated $21 billion valuation, and says annualized revenue now exceeds $1 billion; its growth is often measured by volume traded.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: If volume is inflated by farming, the growth narrative behind a $21 billion valuation is less reliable; diligence should separate organic from wash volume.
insights.locator: Polymarket recently raised an over $1 billion round

insights.claim: Barron's reported that much 2028 US presidential market activity on Polymarket centred on ineligible candidates such as Elon Musk and Zohran Mamdani, and Kalshi was forced to deny wash-trading allegations on its new perpetual futures market for crypto, which Sethi says is explained by market-maker incentives.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Both leading prediction markets face credibility scrutiny; separate genuine incentives (market making) from manipulation when assessing volume.
insights.locator: These types of unusual trading patterns are not a new phenomenon

insights.claim: The CFTC declined to say whether it is examining these election trades; its past Polymarket probes mostly involved potential insider trading rather than wash trading, though it has issued hefty wash-trading fines in other sectors.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: A CFTC enforcement action on wash trading would be a regulatory catalyst for prediction markets; no sign of one yet.
insights.quote: It seems to me that the CFTC would want to know about weird activity in a very large market
insights.locator: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which regulates prediction markets
